newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP urges action to protect fragile wetlands.
newsitem.headline: EP urges action to protect fragile wetlands.

text.p: The European Union should make more money available to protect Europe's fragile wetlands, which are one of the most complex ecosystems in the world, the European Parliament said on Thursday night.

Wetlands not only provide crucial nesting, breeding and feeding grounds for wading and migrating birds and fish, but also perform a whole series of functions which benefit people and the environment, Parliament argued.

These include "regulating the water cycle and controlling floods, checking coastal erosion, storing pollution, nutrient and toxic substances, reducing eutrophication and improving water quality (and) absorbing CO2, thus helping reduce the greenhouse effect," Euro-MPs said in a report.

The report, written by Greek Socialist Angela Kokkola, asked the European Commission to draft an EU policy on conserving wetlands, and urged both the Commission and the member states to make more funds available to protect these areas.
Wetlands were disappearing by being drained for farming and irrigation or altered for tourism, and those that remained were threatened by pollution, the report said.

Euro-MPs said it would be impossible to use wetlands wisely, monitor trends and incorporate wetland policy into other policies without comparable national data giving an inventory of wetlands and their functions.
They asked for a European databank which could be regularly updated.
The report came in response to a Commission communication on wetlands -- COM(95)189.
